News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / West Philippine Sea West Philippine Sea AFP COMMANDS CURRENTLY STAGING ‘REHEARSALS’ NSA chief proposes security plan on Philippine Sea By: Gabryelle Dumalag - @inquirerdotnet Philippine Daily Inquirer / 05:30 AM November 22, 2026 Share: National Security Adviser Eduardo Oban has proposed a five-year security “initiative” on the Philippine Sea involving other allies in the region, as the military steps up efforts to bolster its defense capabilities on the country’s territory, including its waters east of the archipelago.
Oban urged the Philippines to broaden its security priorities beyond the West Philippine Sea (WPS) to include the Philippine Sea and Western Pacific, warning that focusing on only one side of the archipelago could leave other strategic areas vulnerable.

Speaking at the Stratbase Institute’s 11th Pilipinas Conference, Oban said the proposed Philippine Sea Resilience Initiative 2031 would bring together the Philippines and other countries, including Japan, the United States, Australia, South Korea and Palau, in identifying maritime, cyber and infrastructure threats concerning these waters.
Oban said the initiative would focus on four priorities—establishing integrated early-warning systems for maritime, cyber, infrastructure and economic risks; protecting undersea cables and shipping routes; preparing for simultaneous military, cyber, economic and infrastructure disruptions; and developing backup systems to maintain essential national functions during crises.
He said the 2031 target would provide a timeline for translating regional security commitments into measurable capabilities. “By then, we should be able to show that we have reduced vulnerabilities, strengthened crisis response, protected essential functions and preserved greater freedom of action,” Oban said.
Expanding the country’s strategic attention eastward would not diminish its commitment to defending its maritime rights in the WPS, Oban said.
“We must also look east, to the Philippine Sea, where an equally vital part of our security and our future is taking shape,” he said. “Looking east is not turning away from the WPS. It is seeking the whole picture.”
Oban made his recommendations amid the ongoing “rehearsals’ by the Armed Forces of the Philippines simulating the defense of strategic sea routes, islands and offshore energy facilities against external threats.
The 10th AFP Joint Exercise Dagat, Langit at Lupa, which runs until Nov. 27, includes simulated maritime strikes, air and missile defense operations, and efforts to repel hostile landings across operational areas by the Northern Luzon Command, Western Command and National Capital Region Command.
AFP chief Gen. Antonio Nafarrete described the drills as a “mission rehearsal” rather than a routine military exercise, adding that the military would test its operational plans under realistic conditions and identify weaknesses in its ability to conduct joint operations.
“This security environment we face today requires an armed forces that can respond to threats to our sovereignty and territorial integrity,” Nafarrete said during the activity’s opening ceremony Friday at Camp Aguinaldo in Quezon City. “We must be able to bring [our] capabilities together, make timely decisions and carry out operations as one joint force.”
